title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: several DLP policies as triggering events in one Data leaks policy
notes: claim 49: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The multiple-policy capability, 20-policy limit, licensing and roadmap details are supported. The DLP severity control links to instructions for enabling alert notifications, not for selecting High severity; a different cited Microsoft page documents that setting. Two assurances about unchanged data access and user experience also lack explicit supporting text.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management now supports selecting multiple DLP policies as triggering events within a policy.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management is releasing the ability to select multiple Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies as triggering events in a policy.

claims.claim: Previously, administrators could select only one DLP policy as a triggering event.
claims.quote: Previously, admins could only select one DLP policy as a triggering event within Insider Risk Management policies.

claims.claim: A DLP policy is an optional trigger for the Data leaks and Data leaks by priority users templates.
claims.quote:
A DLP policy is optional when using the following policy templates:
- Data leaks
- Data leaks by priority users

claims.claim: The alternative exfiltration-activity triggering event uses selected indicators.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; controls[1].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The DLP triggering-event integration requires High Incident reports severity and does not generate Insider Risk Management alerts from Low or Medium rules.
claims.quote: The *High* severity level is the triggering events and Insider Risk Management alerts aren't generated from rules in DLP policies with the **Incident reports** field set at *Low* or *Medium*.

claims.claim: Low is the default DLP rule report severity.
claims.quote:
The ReportSeverityLevel parameter specifies the severity level of the incident report for content detections based on the rule. Valid values are:
- None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured.
- Low: This value is the default.
- Medium
- High

claims.claim: Only Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and OneDrive for Business DLP alerts are processed by the High Severity DLP Alert indicator.
claims.quote: If your DLP policy spans multiple workloads (for example, Exchange + Endpoint), only the alerts from the supported workloads (Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and OneDrive for Business) are processed.

claims.claim: Policies applying exclusively to Endpoint DLP, Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, on-premises repositories or Power BI do not trigger this indicator.
claims.quote: Alerts generated by DLP policies that apply exclusively to these workloads won't trigger the indicator and won't appear in Insider Risk Management alerts, cases, or activity views:

claims.claim: The Data leaks policy processes high-severity alerts only for users included in both the DLP rule and the insider risk policy.
claims.quote: Only users included in Insider Risk Management policies using the **Data leaks** template have high severity DLP policy alerts processed. Additionally, only users included in a rule for a high severity DLP alert are analyzed by the Insider Risk Management policy for consideration.

claims.claim: High-severity rules in selected DLP policies provide triggering events, subject to the documented user and workload scope.
claims.quote: Whenever a high severity alert is generated by a DLP policy rule and added to the Office 365 audit log, insider risk policies created with this template automatically examine the high severity DLP alert.

claims.claim: An in-scope user's high-severity DLP alert is automatically examined and processed for insider risk scoring.
claims.quote: If the alert contains an in-scope user defined in the insider risk policy, the alert is processed by the insider risk policy as a new alert and assigned an insider risk severity and risk score.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The option does not give Insider Risk Management new content sources or expose data.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "multiple DLP policies" "data sources"'; read policy templates, policy indicators and roadmap description. They describe trigger selection and supported alerts, not an explicit guarantee of unchanged content access.
claims.fix: Replace the Data exposure bullet with 'The option selects which existing DLP alerts start scoring.' Remove 'rather than exposing data' from the risk rationale.

claims.claim: The Purview policy-creation path reaches the Data leaks DLP triggering-event option.
claims.quote: If you select the **User matches a data loss prevention (DLP) policy triggering event** option, you must select a DLP policy from the DLP policy dropdown list to enable triggering indicators for the DLP Policy for this Insider Risk Management policy.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy > Policy template > category > Data leaks > Triggers for this policy > User matches a data loss prevention (DLP) policy triggering event > DLP policy dropdown list'. The guide documents the trigger label; the pre-check's missing-word result is not a wrong label.

claims.claim: No documented Security & Compliance PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation creates or edits Insider Risk Management policies or sets their DLP triggering events.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell Insider Risk Management New-InsiderRiskPolicy Set-InsiderRiskPolicy DLP triggering policies'; 'site:learn.microsoft.com/graph insider risk management policy create update DLP triggering events'. Read scc-powershell and policy workflow; no operation found.

claims.claim: The linked endpoint DLP tutorial documents the path through Incident reports to Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports.
claims.quote: Scroll down to the **Incident reports** section and toggle **Send an alert to admins when a rule match occurs** to **On**.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].ui.docs and the corresponding table link to 'https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-cc-email'. That already-cited page states: 'Under Incident reports, set Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports to High.' The existing endpoint tutorial supports the editing route but does not document the severity control itself; retain the path.

claims.claim: A DLP trigger policy without high-severity alerts does not meet requirements and produces the DLP policy doesn't meet requirements health notification.
claims.quote: | **DLP policy doesn't meet requirements** | - Data leaks - Data leaks by priority users | DLP policies used as triggering events must be configured to generate high severity alerts.

claims.claim: Turning off the DLP policy used as a trigger produces a policy health notification.
claims.quote: | **DLP policy used in this policy is turned off** | - Data leaks - Data leaks by priority users | DLP policy used in this policy is turned off.

claims.claim: Deleting a selected DLP triggering policy produces a policy health notification.

claims.claim: Policy health warns when a triggering event repeatedly occurs for over 15% of users in a policy.
claims.quote: | **Triggering event is repeatedly occurring for over 15% of users in this policy** | All policy templates | Adjust the triggering event to help reduce how often users are brought into the policy scope. |

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft advises prioritizing exfiltration events and selectively assigning High severity.
claims.quote: Prioritize data exfiltration events and be selective when assigning **Incident reports** settings to *High* when configuring rules in your DLP policies.

claims.claim: Raising rule report severity also changes the severity used in DLP admin alerts and reports.
claims.quote: Under **Incident reports**, set **Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports** to **High**.

claims.claim: Users see nothing new as a result of this change.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "multiple DLP policies" "users" "experience"'. Read roadmap description, policy templates and policy workflow. They describe administrator selection and scoring, not an explicit assurance of unchanged end-user experience.
claims.fix: Remove 'users see nothing new, though' and write the impact rationale as 'Low. Insider Risk Management admins and analysts notice it; more users may be scored once more DLP policies feed a policy.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The policy-health monitoring instruction has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Watch each policy's health card for **DLP policy doesn't meet requirements**, **DLP policy used in this policy is turned off** and the over-15%-of-users triggering warning. The table contains only trigger selection, rule severity and role membership.
claims.fix: The first After rollout bullet asks readers to monitor policy health, which has no controls-table row. Remove that bullet; retain the already-supported health facts in Risk assessment and Why it matters. Do not add a new control row.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly state a numerical DLP-policy selection limit for the Data leaks by priority users template.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk Management" "DLP" "20" "priority"'. Read the Data leaks and Data leaks by priority users template sections and Get started step 12. The numerical limit explicitly names Data leaks; the priority-users section refers to its guidelines without stating a number.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Over-assigning High severity to DLP rules can increase Insider Risk Management alert noise and analyst effort.
claims.quote: Over-assigning the *High* level in the **Incident reports** settings in other DLP policy rules can increase the noise in the Insider Risk Management alert workflow and make it more difficult for your data investigators and analysts to properly evaluate these alerts.
